Title: Lilith's Blessing : Propositions for a new text

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
Hello,

As  Johannes mentioned it , I am creating the open revision for Lilith's Blessing cardtext update.

Current text:
Name: Lilith's Blessing
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 1 pool
Master. Put this card in play. As a master phase action, you may tap this card to search your library for a master: Discipline card and choose a ready non-Bahari vampire you control who has no blood. That vampire gains the Discipline card (if any) and 3 blood and becomes Bahari.

How it's going to work
It consists in several steps.
1 - gather propositions.
2 - filter propositions (down to 10).
3 - test propositions.
4 - vote on propositions.
5 - announce result.

How to participate
It's quite simple.
If you want to submit a proposition, send a mail to Rules [at] VampireTheEternalStruggle.com , and set the subject to "[Lilith's Blessing] [Proposition] {a short comment here}" (I can't use <mailto: > here, sadly )
If you want to participate in playtest, send a mail to Rules [at] VampireTheEternalStruggle.com , and set the subject to "[Lilith's Blessing] [Playtest] {your name}" Please also add some information about you: Your name, where you play, how often, and how long you've been playing the game.  If you want to submit feedback, send a mail to Rules [at] VampireTheEternalStruggle.com, and set the subject to "[Lilith's Blessing] [Feedback] {your Id}" (don't be afraid, I'll assign you an Id on reception of your Playtest subscription mail). Feedback will be limited to those who subscribed to the Playtest.  If you want to submit your vote, send a mail to Rules [at] VampireTheEternalStruggle.com, and set the subject to "[Lilith's Blessing] [Vote] {your id}" (same Id you'll be given when subscribing)

A few remarks:

Respect the subjects! I have created filters in may mailbox according to these fields. Anything that doesn't exactly match one of them won't be considered valid. It's easier, safer, better and shorter to copy-paste the text above.

Step 1 : Anyone can submit. You don't have to participate in the playtest to submit.
Step 1 : End date: June 25th. Any propositions received after this date are likely not to be considered in the Step 2.
Step 1 : If a proposition's intent is unclear, depending on how much time I have, I will try to reformulate your idea with you.
Step 1 : Propositions already posted on forums / internet / blogs / ... haven't been taken into account.
Step 1 : Feel free to propose anything. The limits are: changing Lilith's Blessing. Here's an example of something I thought of (but that I don't like): "[Rulebook] Playing a Trifle master card grants you a Trifle Master Phase action. Trifle Master Phase actions can only be used to play Master Cards." (replacing the existing text about Trifles in the Rulebook)
Step 1 : Please send the full text of the card. I can assume it'll remain a master card, but if you want to change the cost, or the requirements (etc.) please make it clear.

A few guidelines:
- The card must remain a Master.
- It's a blessing, not a curse.
- The discipline search is a mandatory part of the effect. (finding doesn't have to be mandatory)
- Here's a short design intent exceprt: "The point is to identify the followers of Lilith (which are the Bahari in WW source material). Lilith, in the source material, rewards those who have suffered."

Step 2 : (filtering X results down to 10) will be achieved by me. Don't get angry if you idea of making it Trifle isn't in there.

Step 3 : Files will be available for Playtest round June 30th. Playtest is open to everyone, but you must register for playtest to receive the versions to playtest.
Step 3 : While testing, feel free to feedback on the version(s) you're testing. Major faults, etc.
Step 3 : There is only one round of playtest. No back-and-forth changes.

Step 4 : I haven't yet decided which voting system to choose. It is likely that I'll ask you to give a mark to the cards you've tested. Now, whether I'll have you give me a preference order, or something else has yet to be decided. One thing seems clear to me, though - it's unlikely we'll go for "relative majority".
Step 4 : Date for vote closure is yet to be announced.

Thanks for having faith, however unfounded it might be. I have been lurking (to simply observe the "design by committee effort) but seem to have been called out. Here's what I can offer.

FORM FOLLOWS FUNCTION: It's crucial to define, gain consensus and clearly state the existing problem BEFORE proposing solutions, so the right bits can be fixed. I believe the issues with Lilith's Blessing were fourfold: simplicity, scale, timing, and persistence.

SIMPLICITY: Villein for everything and Bless became the only correct answer for newly influenced minions. It removed what should have been interesting decision-making.

SCALE: It added too many blood counters to the table. One player in our group often created 2-3 times more blood than Giant's Blood using only LB. Yes, that one player AVERAGED almost 20 additional blood per game throughout our last day-long playing session. And yes, that scale alone did create additional VP. If Giant's Blood is classified as overpowered, what does that make LB in decks made to exploit it?

TIMING: The effect existing in the Master phase leverages Villein's trifle effect too efficiently (regardless of number of MPA)

PERSISTENCE: Once installed, it remained accessible forever (ultimately contributing to scale).

In my mind, that leads to "what can I do with Bahari keywords and skill grafting without contributing to runaway blood creation?" The best course of action might be to parallel an existing set of mechanics. What if LB looked something like Twilight Camp?

And here, despite my earlier rant on consensus-building, I'll offer up a solution that addresses the (admittedly Darby-centric) problem definition above.

Name: Lilith's Blessing
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 1 pool
Master. Put this card in play with 3 blood. During your untap phase, you may tap this card to choose a ready non-Bahari vampire you control. That vampire becomes Bahari. Search your library for a Master: Discipline card. Move up to 3 blood from this card and that Discipline to the chosen vampire. Burn this card when it has no counters.

For templating purposes, I used Jungle Hunting Ground, which actually gains blood, avoiding any "counter to blood" conversion language. The "Search your......chosen vmapire" language is templated from Path of Death and the Soul.

So, this proposal
- gets away from any Villein-Bless (or Vessel-Bless) interaction and keeps the blood gain in the same window as Hunting Grounds or Jake Washington - timing which seems to be currently well-balanced.
- doesn't require an empty vampire, so it can still be done on new minions (after the same waiting period we see with the current LB). You could get the discipline and add one more blood if you want.
- eliminates scale issues - it's post-cost effect is the same as Svadharma or the Coven (the turn it's played) and if used that way, it's gone.
- can remain permanently accessible if you're not harvesting blood, empowering use of "Bahari" and discipline grafting.
- doesn't create any option to use the effect in a combat or response to something like Shattering Crescendo, which I would see as a huge problem (e.g., effectively creating 3 damage prevention for any vampire)
- it remains playable multiple players.

Pascal has seen this proposal, since I submitted as a random voice in the design-by-committee deluge B-)

Darby.

Messages.Author: Rubia
Messages.Body:
It seems I may be too late to suggest a change, but here is my thought on a revision of the card that (in my view) protects the most interesting part of the card and culls much of the abuse:

Lilith's Blessing
Type: Master
Cost: 1 pool
Master. Put this card in play. As a master phase action, you may tap this card to search your library for a master: Discipline card and choose a ready non-Bahari vampire you control who has no blood. That vampire gains the Discipline card (if any) and 3 blood and becomes Bahari.  Burn Lilith's Blessing if you fail to find a Discipline card.

I think this fix stops the widest applications of bloating, unless you are willing to pack your library with discipline cards. Also, it supports my slight bias to encourage the use of discipline cards to increase variety.

Rubia
